diagnosis.summary: Two pods of the `unschedulable` Deployment (unschedulable-7957796bdc-ldzhw and unschedulable-5ddcff94bf-rw5pd) have been stuck in Pending/Unschedulable since 2026-10-04. The cluster has 3 nodes: the control-plane is tainted NoSchedule (and its kubelet is unreachable/NodeStatusUnknown), oncall-worker is Ready but reports 1 node with Insufficient CPU, and oncall-worker2 is Ready but has been cordoned (taint node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable:NoSchedule, unschedulable=True). With the control-plane excluded by taint, worker2 excluded by cordon, and worker1 lacking sufficient CPU, no schedulable node can satisfy the pod's CPU request.

hypotheses.title: oncall-worker2 is cordoned, leaving only one worker with insufficient CPU
hypotheses.mechanism: The scheduler reports 0/3 nodes available: 1 node has the control-plane NoSchedule taint, 1 node (oncall-worker2) carries the node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable:NoSchedule taint (cordoned, unschedulable=True), and 1 node (oncall-worker) has Insufficient CPU for the pod's request. With oncall-worker2 cordoned and oncall-worker unable to fit the CPU request, no node can accept the pods. The cordon on oncall-worker2 appears to have been set deliberately (or left over from maintenance) and was not lifted after the node rebooted.

hypotheses.title: oncall-worker has insufficient CPU to schedule the pods
hypotheses.mechanism: Even if oncall-worker2 were uncordoned, the scheduler reports 1 node with Insufficient CPU (oncall-worker). The pod's CPU request may exceed what is currently allocatable on oncall-worker after existing workloads are accounted for. If the CPU request is too large, pods will remain unschedulable even after the cordon is lifted.

hypotheses.title: oncall-control-plane kubelet is unreachable (NodeStatusUnknown)
hypotheses.mechanism: The control-plane node has had its kubelet stop posting status since 2026-10-05, resulting in NodeStatusUnknown and an added node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoSchedule taint. Combined with the existing control-plane:NoSchedule taint, this node contributes to the pool of unavailable nodes. While control-plane nodes are normally excluded from workload scheduling, the unreachable state means it cannot serve as a fallback even if tolerations were added.
